newsitem.title: USA: US economy may have seen fundamental changes - Guynn.
newsitem.headline: US economy may have seen fundamental changes - Guynn.

text.p: The U.S. economy appears to have undergone fundamental changes that affect the relationship between inflation and the unemployment rate, said Jack Guynn, president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta.
"There are some things that, I think, appear to be very fundamentally different about our economy now," Guynn told the Business Development Board of Palm Beach County.
"For a year or more, we have been seeing a level of unemployment that based on past experience, would have suggested that we would have seen ... much greater inflationary pressures," Guynn said.
Asked about the current levels of U.S. asset markets, Guynn said he saw little evidence that greater investment income from rising stock prices had led to significantly more consumer spending.
"I don't think ... they're spending a great deal of that added wealth," Guynn said.
The regional bank president added, however, that a downturn in the stock market could have an impact on policymakers' views on the economy.
"If we get a correction at some point, it would become a factor in the total equation of gauging the economy," he said.
